overview: Sverker II of Sweden was Swedish king whose reign ended after defeat by the Erik dynasty and death in battle. The profile is anchored by concrete turning points: 1195/96 — Becomes king; 1208 — Defeated at Lena; 1210 — Killed at Gestilren.
He died in 1210, and his reign belongs to the wider story of Scandinavian state formation, Christianization, dynastic conflict, and northern Europe’s ties to England, the Baltic, and the Empire.

contentSections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Sverker II of Sweden was Swedish king whose reign ended after defeat by the Erik dynasty and death in battle. The profile is anchored by concrete turning points: 1195/96 — Becomes king; 1208 — Defeated at Lena; 1210 — Killed at Gestilren.
He died in 1210, and his reign belongs to the wider story of Scandinavian state formation, Christianization, dynastic conflict, and northern Europe’s ties to England, the Baltic, and the Empire.

contentSections.title: Birth and early life
paragraphs: Sverker II of Sweden was born c. 1167. His family background is usually placed in House of Sverker, though early Scandinavian genealogy can be uncertain and politically shaped.

Sverker II of Sweden's early life belonged to the medieval Scandinavian world, where kinship, sea routes, church contacts, assemblies, and armed followings shaped the opportunities available to a ruler.

contentSections.title: Character and Personality
paragraphs: Sverker II of Sweden, of the Sverker dynasty, is remembered through the renewed bloodshed of the Sverker-Erik feud that ultimately destroyed his kingship. The sources present a ruler raised to the throne with the support of powerful magnates and the church, who governed for a time but was then driven out by the rival Erik line and killed in battle at Gestilren in 1210 while attempting to recover his crown.

His reign and fall illustrate the dependence of Swedish kings of the period on aristocratic and ecclesiastical backing, and the deadly instability of the alternating dynasties. He is associated with concessions to the church that strengthened its position in Sweden.

Little of his individual character emerges from the record, which is dominated by the dynastic conflict that defined and ended his reign. He is remembered as a figure in the Sverker-Erik struggle — raised by his backers, deposed by his rivals, and killed in the attempt to return — rather than as a personality recoverable in his own right.

contentSections.title: As king of Sweden
paragraphs: Sverker II ruled Sweden after the Sverker line returned to power. His reign ended amid conflict with Erik Knutsson, including defeat at Lena and later death at Gestilren.
As King of Sweden, Sverker II of Sweden had to turn dynastic claim into workable authority through alliances, military pressure, church support, and acceptance by regional elites.

contentSections.title: Death
paragraphs: Killed at the Battle of Gestilren in 1210 during dynastic conflict with the Erik line.

contentSections.title: Legacy
paragraphs: His career shows the intensity of dynastic politics in early medieval Sweden.
Later saga, saintly, or national traditions often amplified Sverker II of Sweden's reputation, so the article separates near-contemporary evidence from later memory where possible.
